description: A granular player that scatters short grains from a loaded or recorded sound

params.text: Sets how long each grain lasts
Sets how many grains sound at once, while the rate knob is at zero
Sets how far from the playhead the grains are scattered
Sets the pitch the grains are played at
Sets the level of the signal leaving the module
Chooses the shape the level of each grain is faded in and out with
Sets how far the grains are thrown about the stereo field at random
Loads another sound from the directory the current one came from, chosen at random
Records the incoming sound into the buffer, and stops when pressed again
Sets where in the sound the grains are taken from
Sets how many of the grains are played backwards
Sets how fast the playhead walks on its own
Sets a fixed rate for the grains, which takes over from the density knob once it is above zero
Walks the playhead through the sound on its own
Ties the grains to the clock input rather than to the density or rate knobs
Passes the incoming sound straight to the outputs alongside the grains

inputs.text: Added to the position knob, 0V to 10V
Added to the pitch knob, a volt per octave
Added to the grain size knob, 0V to 10V
Added to the grain density knob, 0V to 10V, while the rate knob is at zero
Added to the grain spread knob, 0V to 10V
Added to the pan randomness knob, 0V to 10V
A gate here starts and stops recording
The sound recorded into the buffer
A clock here times the grains while the module is set to follow it
Added to the reverse amount knob, 0V to 10V
Added to the grain rate knob, 0V to 10V; above zero the rate takes over from the density

outputs.text: The left channel of the grains
The right channel of the grains

notes: nothing sounds until the buffer holds something: load a WAV from the right-click menu, drop a WAV file onto the waveform, or patch audio into IN and press the record button
dragging across the waveform moves the playhead, and where it is let go becomes the position knob's setting
menu: Normal Playback (no grains) — plays the buffer straight through instead of scattering grains from it
Silence Threshold — sets the level below which Remove Silence counts a sample as silent
Remove Silence — deletes every sample in the buffer quieter than the silence threshold
Normalize WAV — scales the buffer so its loudest sample reaches full scale
Load WAV... — opens a file dialogue and reads a WAV into the buffer
Save Buffer as WAV... — writes what is in the buffer to a stereo WAV file

inputs.1: 1V per octave · continuous · one channel only
inputs.6: high above 0.5V · stepped · one channel only
inputs.8: high above 1V · stepped · one channel only
